source_decision.reason: Statsig gates, dynamic configs, experiments, metrics, holdouts, layers, segments, ingestion jobs, prompts, releases, and administrative resources are feature-control, experimentation, analytics, or project-management control-plane objects. The official contract does not prove a canonical task, note, or user-work project Source with a durable version and honest deletion or tombstone model.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Console API Keys are Statsig's most powerful key type and can perform full CRUD across the project.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Uses one encrypted header-auth connection, exposes no credential argument, pins the version header, requires approval on every mutation, and keeps all outputs private by default.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Statsig documents one Console API origin; per-organization vendor-tag connection matching would allow a Statsig-tagged credential record on a different host.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Omits per_org from the connection requirement so enrollment matches the exact statsigapi.net host, while every operation remains fixed to the same origin-only base.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Key list, create, read, update, delete, deactivate, and rotate responses can contain plaintext client, server, Console, SCIM, or organization API keys; five item routes also carry the key identifier in the path.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Retains the complete key-management capability with every key mutation approval-gated, but labels all seven responses and all five path-bearing requests sensitive, warns against reusable configuration or URL disclosure, and excludes both key GETs from bundled rendering workflows.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Databricks ingestion and warehouse-connection updates can carry access tokens, passwords, service-account private keys, and SSH private keys in request bodies.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Keeps the full operations but marks body_raw as secret material, requires approval, emits no workflow over either route, and configures no hidden retry.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Gate, dynamic-config, experiment, layer, holdout, release, segment, key, and ingestion actions can change live targeting, exposure, access, or data-processing state.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Classifies deletes and high-impact lifecycle, override, key, and credential actions as destructive; every mutation is approval-gated and non-GET responses are never cached.

audit_findings_folded.finding: The official OpenAPI defines no operationId for any of its 313 operations.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Derives deterministic names from the primary official tag, HTTP method, and official summary, proves uniqueness across the complete pinned inventory, and records the formula and IDs in the fixture.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Forty-seven collections expose one-based limit/page controls, ingestion runs exposes page without a caller-set size, and Logs Explorer uses an opaque cursor with a documented 100 default and 1000 maximum; the dynamic-config review list has no documented success body.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Automatically owns 46 complete limit/page contracts plus ingestion and Logs, uses distinct bounded offset-page and query-token declarations, and extracts the exact records path including segment data.ids. The undocumented review-list response remains caller-paged and makes no completeness claim.

audit_findings_folded.finding: The billing report returns CSV rather than JSON.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Captures the response as a private text/csv file_ref with a stable filename; bytes never enter ordinary recipe values or JSON parsing.

audit_findings_folded.finding: All 127 request bodies are required JSON: 120 object schemas, six object-union schemas, and one array schema.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Every body uses required bounded body_raw with an authority-derived object or array wire-root pattern, preserving union branches, nested fields, nulls, and exact integer lexemes.

audit_findings_folded.finding: DELETE /console/v1/segments/{id}/id_list requires a JSON body naming the segment IDs to remove.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Admits the route with required bounded object body_raw and Content-Type application/json; the raw-body transport is preserved on DELETE and the audit regression prevents accidental body omission.

audit_findings_folded.finding: The OpenAPI includes many int64 timestamps, durations, and counts, and several integer query parameters can exceed safe JavaScript integer precision.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Parses all JSON response integers losslessly, sends JSON bodies verbatim, and exposes scalar integer parameters as validated decimal strings while preserving documented nonnegative and positive minima in their patterns.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Statsig documents project mutation limits of about 100 requests per 10 seconds and 900 per 15 minutes.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Declares no hidden retry or mutation fan-out; each operation is one provider call and rate-limit failures surface to the caller.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Statsig feature-control and experimentation objects resemble work resources but lack honest canonical task, note, or user-work project deletion semantics.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Declares no work_entity_sources and records the semantic rejection in the evidence fixture.
